increments.title: Copy as new: the backend writes both aggregates in one idempotent call
increments.diagnosis:
Diagnosis re-verified against the current tree (frontend HEAD 8340a95c) and it still holds in full. Frontend `src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:31-46` — `copy` fetches `${notificationFulfilmentsUrl}/${journeyId}/copy` once with an `Idempotency-Key` header and marshals the response; nothing writes the notification side. Backend `NotificationFulfilmentsService.copy(id, idempotencyKey)` dedupes by key, guards copyable status, then loops `referenceNumberGenerator.generate()` + `notificationFulfilmentsRepository.insert(copy)` and returns — the `notification` collection is never touched. Consequences confirmed in code: the dashboard lists from `GET /notifications` (`read.js:22-48`, no aggregation join, `marshalListItem` reads `referenceNumber/commodity/origin/transport.arrivalDate/consignor/consignee` from the notification side only); the first save POSTs `/notifications` with `referenceNumber` set (`mutate.js:36-46`), which `NotificationService.saveOriginOfImport` routes to `updateNotification`, which throws `NotFoundException` for an unknown reference; `put-projection.js` retries the same body and rethrows, so it is a hard recoverable-error page; `transition.js` dual-posts submit/amend/cancel-amend/soft-delete to `/notifications/{ref}/...`, all 404 for a copy.

The corrected diagnosis's extra point — copy SEMANTICS diverge between the two aggregates — is also still true and is now RESOLVED by this spec rather than left open. `NotificationCopyMapper.toCopyDto` resets transport, consignment, `internalReference`, per-animal counts/species and `unweanedAnimals`; the fulfilments copy retains everything, and so does the stub adapter. Post-retrofit the Notification is a derived projection of the fulfilments (`mutate.js` re-projects every field from the canonical snapshot on every save), so a reset applied only to the projection is not a product behaviour at all — it is a projection that disagrees with the answers the user can see in the hub, and it is silently erased by the first save. A durable reset would have to drop the corresponding entries from the canonical fulfilments, which needs frontend-owned obligation ids inside the backend and is out of scope. This spec therefore copies the source Notification VERBATIM at the new reference, which (a) keeps projection and canonical aggregate consistent, (b) matches the stub adapter, whose behavioural parity with the real adapter is a standing obligation on this increment, and (c) matches what the existing E2E specs already assert about a copy carrying the source's answers. `NotificationCopyMapper` and its reset semantics become dead and are deleted; the product-visible consequence is flagged in openQuestions.

Also verified for the file list: no ArchUnit/package-boundary tests exist in the backend, so `notificationfulfilments` may depend on `notification` (it already imports `ReferenceNumberGenerator` from it); `MongoConfig` registers a `MongoTransactionManager`, so the existing `@Transactional` on `copy` really does span both writes; the real integration test is `integration/NotificationFulfilmentsIT.java` (NOT the placeholder name in the old spec) and it already autowires `NotificationRepository`; `NotificationFulfilmentsServiceTest` hand-builds the service in `setUp`, so a new collaborator means editing that file.
increments.refutation:
I tried to break this on all five fronts and could not. Every cited line is accurate.

DEFECT EXISTS. frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:31-46 — real-mode `copy` makes exactly one fetch, POST `${notificationFulfilmentsUrl}/${journeyId}/copy`, and returns marshal() of that response. Contrast `create` at lines 11-29 which POSTs /notifications first (backend mints the ref) then PUTs the fulfilments aggregate at that same ref; the comment at lines 7-10 states the ordering as a rule. backend:.../notificationfulfilments/NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:85-128 confirms copy() mints its own ref via referenceNumberGenerator.generate() and calls only notificationFulfilmentsRepository.insert(copy) — no Notification is written. Real mode is the default (frontend:src/server/app/services/mode.js:1, `process.env.LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE ?? 'real'`) and the stack sets it explicitly (docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml:52). Not already-fixed, not cannot-reproduce.

ROOT CAUSE, NOT SYMPTOM. I looked one level down for an escape hatch and there is none. The dashboard list is purely notification-side: read.js:22-48 fetches `${notificationsUrl}?page=...` with no aggregation join, and the comment at 16-21 says so. The save path mutate.js:36-46 POSTs /notifications with `referenceNumber: journeyId` set, which backend NotificationService.java:85-92 (saveOriginOfImport) routes to updateNotification, and updateNotification at 380-384 throws NotFoundException for an unknown reference. I checked whether the retry wrapper rescues it: real/projections/put-projection.js:17-38 retries the identical body MAX_PROJECTION_ATTEMPTS times and then rethrows — there is no 404-to-create fallback, so the first save of a copy is a hard recoverable-error page. transition.js:23-83 confirms finalise/amend/cancelAmend/softDelete each dual-post to `${notificationsUrl}/${journeyId}/...`, all of which 404 for a copy. I also checked for a way to fix this purely in the frontend while keeping the idempotent call: NotificationController.java exposes only POST /notifications, POST /{ref}/copy, /submit, /amend, /cancel-amend, /soft-delete, GET, DELETE — there is NO PUT /notifications/{ref} upsert. So the frontend genuinely cannot create a Notification at a ref the fulfilments copy already minted. The needs-decision framing survives that attack.

MATCHES THE SNAG. "Copy as new is broken" — the copy vanishes from the dashboard and dies on first save. That is the reporter's complaint.

VERDICT IS RIGHT, AND FOR THE RIGHT REASON. The idempotency machinery is real and load-bearing: notification-actions/controller.js:26-42 reads a hidden idempotencyKey from the payload, and recoverCopy at 12-24 re-renders the dashboard or notification view with the SAME key preserved on a recoverable 500, so the user's retry dedupes at NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:88-95 (findCopy by idempotency key). The notification-side copy endpoint has no key. So option (a) really does trade retry-safety for the fix, and option (b) really does require a backend change. Two defensible answers in different repos = needs-decision, correctly called.

ONE SUBSTANTIVE GAP the investigator missed (see correctedDiagnosis) — copy SEMANTICS diverge between the two aggregates, which adds a third dimension to the gate decision and means option (a) is not the clean "restore pre-retrofit ordering" it is billed as.

REPO LIST is complete. frontend + tests under option (a); frontend + backend + tests under option (b). Nothing else consumes the copy path — admin reads notifications but does not copy, and the stub repo is uninvolved.

increments.notes:
Real-mode "Copy as new" creates only the canonical notification-fulfilments document and never the paired Notification record at the copy's new reference. The copy therefore never appears on the dashboard (which lists from /notifications), and the first save, submit, amend or delete of the copy 404s on the notification side and surfaces the recoverable-error page. Introduced by the EUDPA-288 retrofit (23f2fdb4), which swapped the pre-retrofit POST /notifications/{ref}/copy for POST /notification-fulfilments/{id}/copy without restoring the notification-side write. Invisible to the frontend's own suites because they run in stub mode, where one in-memory map backs both reads. The defect is unambiguous; the fix shape is a design call, because the only idempotent copy endpoint is the fulfilments one and the only reference-minting endpoint the dashboard reads from is the notification one.

RED-BEFORE-GREEN: step 3 is the gate. Write the new NotificationFulfilmentsIT tests FIRST, run step 3, and record it FAILING before touching any main-source file. It fails on today's tree because no Notification exists at the copy's reference. Step 11 is the second red-today check: the extended dashboard card assertion and the submit-the-copy leg both fail against the current stack. The frontend's own vitest and Playwright suites pin LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE=stub (vitest.config.js:12, playwright.config.js:60), so steps 5-6 can never go red for this snag — they are regression guards only, not proof.

DECISIONS TAKEN (record these on the ticket):
1. Which endpoint carries the dual write — the existing POST /notification-fulfilments/{id}/copy. The frontend already sends exactly one idempotent call there, so the ruling's 'backend-owned single idempotent call' is satisfied with zero frontend production change. The endpoint shape is untouched, so the REST-noun nudge in the ruling does not fire.
2. Copy semantics — VERBATIM, not NotificationCopyMapper's reset. Post-retrofit the Notification is a projection of the canonical fulfilments; a reset applied only to the projection disagrees with the hub the user sees and is erased by the first save (mutate.js re-projects every field). A durable reset would have to drop entries from the canonical fulfilments, which needs frontend-owned obligation ids inside the backend. Verbatim also keeps the stub adapter (stub/lifecycle/create.js, structuredClone of the source) behaviourally aligned with real — a standing obligation on this increment. Reversal path if product wants the reset back: apply it to the fulfilments copy, not the projection.
3. Deleting POST /notifications/{ref}/copy, NotificationService.copyNotification and NotificationCopyMapper — they become dead with decision 2, and the endpoint is itself a half-write (a Notification with no fulfilments document) that recreates this class of bug. Verified no consumer in any of the 10 workspace repos; the tests-repo API client's copyNotification method is also unreferenced and goes with it.
4. Missing-source fallback — if the fulfilments document being copied has no paired Notification (the orphan population this very bug created), the copy still gets an empty DRAFT Notification at its reference rather than a hard failure, so it is listable and self-heals on first save.

DO NOT CHANGE: real/lifecycle/create.js and its test at real.requests.test.js:358-370 — the single call with the Idempotency-Key is now the correct behaviour, not the defect. An implementor working from the pre-ruling spec would 'fix' it into a two-call sequence; that is option (a), which the ruling rejected.

Branch fix/EUDPA-317-copy-as-new-missing-notification must exist with that exact name in all three repos (workspace rule 2) — use `tim workspace branch`. Backend ITs run under Failsafe at verify, never `mvn test`. Run `npm run format` in the frontend and tests repos before committing (pre-commit hooks enforce format + lint). No migration or rationale comments in the changed code; the why lives here and on the ticket.

This matches the stub adapter and the canonical fulfilments, which have always been copied whole, but it is a visible change from main's notification-side behaviour. If a reset is still wanted, it must be applied to the canonical fulfilments copy and specified per obligation, as a separate increment.

Are there already-copied notifications in any deployed environment holding orphaned notification-fulfilments documents with no Notification row? The fallback in this increment only helps copies made after it ships; existing orphans still need a backfill-or-discard decision.
Should the strengthened dashboard assertion stay tagged @smoke, given it adds a dashboard round-trip and a search to a path already marked test.slow()?
increments.ruling: RULED 2026-08-10 (Sam: look at what main did before the rewrite). Pre-retrofit, src/server/notification-copy/controller.js made ONE call — notificationClient.copy -> POST /notifications/{ref}/copy — and the backend returned the new notification with its reference already minted. There was no frontend dual write and no Idempotency-Key header. So option (b), a backend-owned single idempotent call, RESTORES the original architecture; option (a) would invent a frontend dual write that never existed here. The action-path endpoint shape is pre-existing rather than newly introduced, though the REST guide would prefer a noun if it is being touched anyway. The only genuinely new decision is whether to keep the retrofit's Idempotency-Key retry semantics: keep them, they are strictly better than the original.

increments.snagText: Copy as new CSS is off
increments.title: Stop .app-link-button resetting font-family so link-buttons render in GDS Transport
increments.diagnosis:
"Copy as new" on the notification dashboard renders in the browser's default serif (Times) while every action next to it renders in GDS Transport. The cause is a single conflicting declaration in the custom stylesheet.

WHERE THE ELEMENT IS
`frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:91-106` renders each summary-card action two ways. Actions carrying an `href` render as `<a class="govuk-link">`; actions carrying a `postAction` render as `<button type="submit" class="govuk-link app-link-button">` inside a `<form class="app-form-inline">` (CSRF crumb + idempotency key must be POSTed, so it cannot be an anchor). `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:19-24` gives the copy action a `postAction`, so on a DRAFT row "Copy as new" is the ONLY `<button>` among Resume / Delete anchors — it is visibly the odd one out, which is exactly what "CSS is off" describes. (On a SUBMITTED row "Amend" is a button too, so it is affected identically.)

ROOT CAUSE — cascade conflict on font-family
`frontend:src/client/stylesheets/core/_main.scss:16` declares `font-family: inherit` on `.app-link-button`. govuk-frontend 6.4.0 declares `font-family: GDS Transport, arial, sans-serif` on `.govuk-link, a`. Both selectors are specificity 0-1-0, so source order decides. Verified in the built bundle `frontend:.public/stylesheets/application.1ee130c.min.css`:
  - byte 941  → `.govuk-link,a{font-family:GDS Transport,arial,sans-serif;...}`
  - byte 1080 → the same rule again
  - byte 137469 → `.app-link-button{background:none;border:none;padding:0;cursor:pointer;font-size:inherit;font-family:inherit;font-weight:inherit;display:inline;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:inherit;color:var(--govuk-link-colour,#1a65a6)}`
`.app-link-button` is emitted last (application.scss `@use` order: `govuk-frontend` then `variables`/`helpers`/`core`), so `font-family: inherit` wins on the `<button>` and defeats `.govuk-link`.

WHY `inherit` RESOLVES TO SERIF
govuk-frontend 6.4.0 sets font-family per component class only — there is no global rule to inherit from. Proof: `grep -o "body{[^}]*}"` on the built bundle returns exactly `body{margin:0;background-color:var(--govuk-body-background-colour,#fff)}`, and `.govuk-template` emits only background-colour / text-size-adjust / scroll-padding / overflow. The full inventory of `font-family:GDS Transport` rules in the bundle (53 of them, captured at `~/git/defra/trade-imports-animals/workareas/shared/frontend-snagging-eudpa315/gdsfont.txt`) contains `.govuk-summary-card__title` but NOT `.govuk-summary-card`, `.govuk-summary-card__title-wrapper`, `.govuk-summary-card__actions` or `.govuk-summary-card__action`. So no ancestor of the button supplies a family, `inherit` falls through to the root initial value, and Chrome computes `Times`. A previous live check at 1440px recorded exactly this: `.app-link-button` computed `Times` while its sibling `a.govuk-link` in the same `<ul>` computed `"GDS Transport", arial, sans-serif`.

WHY THE OTHER DECLARATIONS ARE FINE — `font-size: inherit`, `font-weight: inherit` and `line-height: inherit` do NOT conflict, because `.govuk-link` sets none of them; the button correctly inherits size 19 and bold from `.govuk-summary-card__actions` (bundle byte ~229 of the summary-card mixin sets `govuk-font-size(19)` + `govuk-typography-weight-bold`). `font-family` is the only broken declaration. The explicit `color` override at `_main.scss:23` is correct and load-bearing (govuk sets link colour via `:link`, which never matches `<button>`) and must stay.

BLAST RADIUS — the same defect affects every `.app-link-button` in the app, all of which also carry `.govuk-link`: `features/commodities/consignment-details/_selected-commodities-table.njk:8`, `features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:19`, `features/documents/contracts/remove-action.js:12`. One stylesheet edit fixes all of them.

ALTERNATIVE RULED OUT — a wrapping/width theory (that the action row wraps because `frontend:src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:57` hard-codes `govuk-grid-column-two-thirds` where the pre-retrofit layout used `govuk-grid-column-full`). That width regression is real and worth its own ticket, but it is a whole-page layout change affecting every screen — it does not single out "Copy as new", and fixing it would leave the button still rendering in Times. The font-family conflict is the defect that makes this one element, and only this element, look wrong.
increments.refutation:
I attacked this on all five fronts and could not break it. It survives, and I was able to upgrade the evidence from static to live-measured.

FRONT 1 — DOES THE DEFECT EXIST? Yes, verified in source and at runtime.
`frontend:src/client/stylesheets/core/_main.scss:11-32` contains the `.app-link-button` rule, and line 17 is `font-family: inherit;` — the only `font-family` declaration in the entire app source (`grep -rn "font-family" src/client/ src/server/` returns exactly that one hit). The built bundle agrees: `grep -o "app-link-button{[^}]*}" .public/stylesheets/application.*.min.css` emits `...font-size:inherit;font-family:inherit;font-weight:inherit;...`.

I then measured it live. The stack is up on :3000, so I loaded a frontend-rendered page (`http://localhost:3000/definitely-not-a-real-page`, 404 via `shared/layout.njk`, so the real `application.css` is the only stylesheet loaded) and injected the exact DOM the dashboard emits — `.govuk-summary-card > .govuk-summary-card__title-wrapper > ul.govuk-summary-card__actions > li.govuk-summary-card__action > form.app-form-inline > button.govuk-link.app-link-button`, alongside a sibling `a.govuk-link`. Computed styles:
  button → fontFamily `Times`, fontSize 19px, fontWeight 700, lineHeight 25px, color rgb(26,101,166)
  link   → fontFamily `"GDS Transport", arial, sans-serif`, fontSize 19px, fontWeight 700, lineHeight 25px, color rgb(26,101,166)
Font-family is the ONLY divergent property, exactly as diagnosed. That also independently confirms the investigator's "the other `inherit` declarations are fine" claim rather than taking it on trust.

FRONT 2 — ROOT CAUSE OR SYMPTOM? Root cause, and the mechanism checks out one level up and one level down.
Up: I traced why `inherit` resolves to serif rather than trusting the bundle grep. `govuk-frontend@6.4.0` (`node_modules/govuk-frontend/package.json:4`) applies typography per component class only. `objects/_template.mixin.scss:45-51` gives `<body>` (`.govuk-template__body`) only `margin: 0` + `background-color` — confirmed in the bundle (`govuk-template__body{margin:0;background-color:var(--govuk-body-background-colour,#fff)}`). `core/_global-styles.mixin.scss` adds only `a { @extend %govuk-link }` and `p { @extend %govuk-body-m }` — that is where the bundle's `.govuk-link,a` selector comes from, and it does not touch `body`. `components/summary-list/_mixin.scss:229-231` gives `.govuk-summary-card__actions` `govuk-font-size(19)` + `govuk-typography-weight-bold` but NO family; `:245` gives `.govuk-summary-card__action` only `display`. The correction is to the decision being asked for. The investigator frames it as an unruled product choice between "today-or-later" and "strictly future". The workspace's own trace-mined legacy specs show the analogous IPAFFS rule is a WINDOW THAT PERMITS PAST DATES — CHED-D is "5 days in the past or 120 days in the future" (workareas/trace-requirements/ched-d/journey-spec.json:7939, evidenced against legacy `arrival_date_validator.js:43-49` with a per-CHED-type `futureDateLimit` at `:18-22`) and CHED-P is "30 days in the past or 180 days in the future" (ched-p/journey-spec.json:16573). Live animals is CHED-A and has no trace file, so the specific numbers are genuinely unknown — which is why needs-decision still stands — but the question to put to product is "what is the CHED-A arrival/exit/issue window, and can we recover it from the legacy validator's per-type table?", not a choice between two future-only rules. increments.title: Restore enhanced search/autocomplete on the long select and picker lists
increments.diagnosis:
The snag is a known, deliberate regression introduced by the EUDPA-288 retrofit, not an accident.

1. The enhancement was removed on purpose. `git -C repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend show --stat bc285d71` (contained in the retrofit merge 23f2fdb4) is titled "refactor(EUDPA-288): drop accessible-autocomplete for plain selects; commodity checkboxes (p-236)". Its message: "origin country and port of entry keep their server-rendered govukSelects with the enhancement stripped; transit countries becomes a single 31-country govuk checkboxes group; commodity selection renders all eight commodity-species pairs as grouped checkboxes with the whole search/filter/carry/summary apparatus removed. accessible-autocomplete dependency, bundle entry, scss import and all data attributes deleted. … Enhanced search returns as a later round." It cites AUTOCOMPLETE-ASSESSMENT.md (not present in any repo or workarea — I searched) and "Sam's ruling". The prototype work it reverted is commits 7edced0d (inc-058, country-of-origin canary) and b79c1379 (inc-059, port-of-entry rollout).

2. Current state confirmed by reading the code, not inferred:
- `grep -rn "data-select-autocomplete\|selectAutocomplete" src webpack.config.js` returns nothing. `webpack.config.js:22-30` has only `application` and `documents` entries; `src/client/javascripts/` contains only `application.js`. `accessible-autocomplete` is absent from `package.json`.
- frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:18 renders a bare `govukSelect` over `services/ports`, whose fixture `src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json` holds 78 records — an 80-option native dropdown once placeholder + divider are counted. That is the single worst "clunky" surface and squarely against GDS guidance for long option lists.
- frontend:.../features/origin/template.njk:15, .../destination-country/template.njk:13, .../port-of-exit/template.njk:13 and .../addresses/create-address/create-address.njk:68 are the same pattern over the 31-country fixtures (`countries-origin.json`, `countries.json`), i.e. 33 options each.
- frontend:.../transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.njk:16 is one flat 31-item checkbox group.
- frontend:.../commodities/search/search.njk is still named and keyed "search" (copy.en.js:4 `search:`) but contains no search box at all — just grouped checkboxes (search.njk:19-29). The controller `search.controller.js` has no query handling. A page called "search" with nothing to search in is exactly what a snagger would flag.

3. The one genuine free-text search left — the address-book party picker — is also clunky by design and carries a real, untested defect:
- `_address-picker.njk:8-12` states the intent: "no client JS anywhere". Search is a secondary submit button (`_address-picker.njk:86-91`) causing a full-page POST; results are `PAGE_SIZE = 5` (`src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:26`) over 40 records = 8 pages.
- Pagination is server-rendered `<a href>` links whose query string is baked at render time from the render-time `selectedId` and `query` (`.../party-picker/view-model/index.js:33-38` → `view-model/pagination/results-href.js:3-13`). Because there is no client JS to sync them, a radio the user ticks — or a query they type — on the current page is silently discarded the moment they click a page link. The hidden `selected` field (`_address-picker.njk:73-75`) is likewise render-time only.
- No test covers this. `hub-picker.e2e.spec.js:251` ("carries a later-page selection…") pages FIRST and ticks SECOND, so it never exercises tick-then-page. `party-picker.controller.test.js:80-95` asserts only that the server bakes the *incoming* `selected` into the hrefs.

4. The fix is two-repo whichever way the gate is answered: the -tests suite has specs written specifically to pin the stripped state — `tests/e2e/features/port-of-entry-select.spec.ts:16` asserts `option` `toHaveCount(80)` under the describe "Port of entry plain select", and `tests/e2e/features/country-of-origin-select.spec.ts:13` asserts `toHaveCount(33)` under "Country of origin plain select". Restoring the enhancement invalidates both.

Why this is not actionable: "clunky af" does not say which surface, and the only mechanism that would fix it was removed by an explicit written assessment plus a named ruling. Reinstating it without a fresh ruling is re-litigating a closed decision by guesswork, and the scope varies enormously by answer (one webpack entry and two templates, versus five templates plus transit-countries plus the commodity page plus a client-side picker). The picker's lose-your-selection-on-paginate bug is the one sub-item that is unconditionally wrong and could be built today, but it is a fragment of the snag, not the snag.

2. The break point. tests:page-objects/base/base-page.ts:81 `return \`/notifications/${journeyId}${suffix}\`` and :85 `pathname.match(/^\/notifications\/([^/]+)/)` are set-prefix-blind, throwing at :87. `tim workspace status --json` puts tests on `fix/EUDPA-319-hub-commodity-totals-boxes` (main lineage).

The diagnosis's headline claim — "it is NOT an accessibility defect" — was asserted, not evidenced. All four failures die BEFORE any scan (three at base-page.ts:87, one at notification-view-page.ts:47 then `No accessibility scans were run` at fixtures/a11y.ts:78). "axe never ran" is not the same as "axe would find nothing", so those pages could still have carried real WCAG violations and the ladder's step 7 "expect 12 passed, 0 failed" was a guess.

I settled it. I cut a git worktree of tests `spike/trace-to-requirements` (the branch whose page objects match the running image), symlinked node_modules, and ran all six live-animals a11y specs against the untouched running stack — no reseed, no stack rebuild, siblings undisturbed. Result: 6 of 6 green (3 journey-state specs 45.3s; view-states + dashboard-views + 1 pre-existing skip 7.3s). Zero axe violations on the pages that had never been scanned. My run collapses one arm of the gate to zero work: against the prefixed build, the matching tests branch is already 100% green, so if "the prefixed build" is the target there is no snag fix at all — only a workspace alignment (`tim workspace branch`), not a 66-file port. The other arm (rebuild the stack from local repos/ so the un-prefixed main build is served) is still untested by anyone, and testing it means rebuilding a stack five sibling agents are mid-run against. Which world EUDPA-315 is snagging is a human call about programme sequencing, and it swings the outcome between "no code" and "back-port set-base awareness onto main-lineage tests". That is a decision, not an implementable fix. `actionable` would be wrong.

The proposed guard `tests:tests/e2e/features/route-base-parity.spec.ts` would not fire in the lane the snag names. package.json:28 defines `test:docker-compose:a11y` as `--grep '@a11y'`, and e2e feature specs carry no such tag (verified: `grep -n "@a11y" tests/e2e/features/reference-strip.spec.ts` returns nothing).
